title: Global Health GIS Professional in the Age of AI
subtitle: From Maps to Impact: Geospatial Intelligence for a Healthier, More Equitable World
question: How can a global health GIS professional evolve within the age of AI and data science to create greater impact, while advancing responsible, equitable, and ethical use of GeoAI for global health?
context: Source text: the supplied Six-Thinking-Hats-GPT graphic, transcribed in book/graphic-text.md with normalized line wrapping. Purple focus records its Role; Purple items record its six Key Outputs. Its tagline is “Integrate • Synthesize • See the Bigger Picture”. Surrounding decorative callouts remain in the image and full text transcription.
demo_notice: SOURCE RECONSTRUCTION — these are the graphic’s statements, questions, and aspirations, not verified findings. Purple describes a role and desired outputs, not a completed synthesis. SVG cards reconstruct content and connections, not the globe or hat artwork.

black.label: Black Hat — Risks & Challenges
black.focus: What could go wrong? What are the limitations?
items: AI may automate parts of traditional GIS work
Risk of spatial bias, false precision, and model misuse
Geoprivacy and re-identification risks (especially for HIV and key populations)
Data quality and underrepresentation of vulnerable regions
Technical and computational constraints (e.g., JupyterLite limits)
Ethical, legal, and data governance challenges
Sustainability, funding, and career uncertainty
questions: What are the biggest risks to my career and impact?
